subject: biology
title: Osmosis
key_idea: **Osmosis** is the movement of water from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane. It needs no energy. It makes plant and animal cells gain or lose water, depending on the solution around them.

blocks.text: Osmosis is the movement of water across a membrane. This section covers the key words and the direction water moves.

items.meaning: A membrane that lets some particles through and stops others, such as a cell membrane.
Lots of water, little dissolved substance.
The movement of water from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane.
How likely water is to move. Pure water is highest, and dissolved substances lower it.

items: Small water molecules pass through the membrane. Larger solute molecules, such as sugar, do not.
Water moves from a high water potential to a low water potential. This is the same direction as dilute to concentrated.
Water keeps moving until the two sides balance.
Osmosis is **passive**: it needs no energy. Active transport does need energy.

items.text: Osmosis happens only across a partially permeable membrane.
Decide which side is more dilute and which is more concentrated.
Water moves from the dilute side to the concentrated side. The dissolved substance does not cross.
The concentrated side gains water. A bag or cell on that side swells.

blocks.text: A common model is a bag of membrane filled with sugar solution and placed in water. Water moves in because the solution inside is more concentrated, so the bag swells.

items: Osmosis moves water, not solute.
Water moves from dilute to concentrated, or high to low water potential.
It is passive and needs no energy.

sections.heading: Osmosis in plant and animal cells

blocks.text: A cell acts like the bag in the model, so what happens depends on the solution around it.

items.meaning: A plant cell full of water, pushing firmly against its cell wall.
A plant cell that has lost so much water that the cytoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall.
An animal cell swelling with water until it bursts.

rows: More dilute than the cell, such as pure water
Water enters. The vacuole swells and the cell becomes **turgid**. The cell wall stops it bursting.
Water enters. The cell swells and bursts (**lysis**). There is no cell wall.
No net movement of water. The cell stays the same.
No net movement of water. The cell stays the same.
Water leaves. The cell is **plasmolysed** and limp.
Water leaves. The cell shrinks and shrivels (it crenates).

items: Turgid cells push against each other and support the plant. Without enough water the plant wilts.
Root hair cells take in water from the soil by osmosis.
Stomata open when glucose builds up in the guard cells. Water enters them by osmosis, they swell and curve, and the stoma opens.
In untreated diabetes the blood has too much glucose. It is more concentrated than the body cells, so water leaves the cells by osmosis.
Dilute outside: a plant cell becomes turgid and an animal cell bursts.
Concentrated outside: a plant cell is plasmolysed and an animal cell shrivels.
The cell wall is why a plant cell does not burst.

blocks.text: Put pieces of plant tissue in solutions of different concentrations. Weigh each piece before and after. A gain in mass means water entered. A loss means water left.
Pieces start with different masses, so compare using **percentage change**. A gain is positive and a loss is negative.

blocks.label: Percentage change in mass
blocks.formula: percentage change in mass = (change in mass ÷ starting mass) × 100
where: change in mass = final mass − starting mass, in g

items.text: A potato piece goes from 2.5 g to 2.7 g. The change is 2.7 − 2.5 = 0.2 g.

blocks.label: Rate of water uptake
blocks.formula: rate of water uptake = amount of water taken in ÷ time taken
where: amount of water, in g or cm³

diagram.alt: A line graph of change in mass of potato tissue against concentration of solution. The line falls from a gain in mass in pure water, crosses the no-change level at about 0.3 mol per dm cubed, and then falls to a loss in mass in concentrated solutions.

y.label: Change in mass of the tissue

items: Plot percentage change in mass against concentration.
Where the line crosses zero there is no net movement of water.
That solution has the same concentration as the solution inside the cells.
The full method is in the required practical note.
Gain in mass: water entered. Loss in mass: water left.
Use percentage change to compare pieces of different mass.
The zero crossing on the graph shows the concentration inside the cells.

checks.a: The movement (diffusion) of water from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane.

checks.q: A plant cell is placed in a concentrated sugar solution. Describe and explain what happens to the cell.
checks.a: Water leaves the cell by osmosis, because the solution outside is more concentrated than inside. The cytoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall and the cell is plasmolysed.

checks.q: A potato piece has a mass of 8.0 g. After 24 hours in water it has a mass of 8.4 g. Calculate the percentage change in mass.

worked_example.question:
A student carried out an investigation using chicken eggs, placing each egg into a separate beaker containing 200 cm3 of distilled water. The masses of the eggs increased.

Explain why the masses of the eggs increased.
answer_points: Water entered the egg by osmosis.
Water moved from a dilute solution in the beaker (distilled water) to a more concentrated solution in the egg cell.
The water moved through a partially permeable membrane.
worked_example.tip: Each point is one mark. Say concentration (or water concentration or water potential), never the amount of water.

worked_example.question:
Potato chip A is transferred from the distilled water into a concentrated salt solution.

Explain what will happen to the cells in potato chip A.
answer_points: The cells lose water and become plasmolysed.
The water moves out by osmosis.
It moves from a high concentration of water molecules in the potato to a low concentration of water molecules in the salt solution, through the partially permeable membrane.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the outcome, one for osmosis and one for the direction of movement across the membrane.

worked_example.question:
Red blood cells burst when they are placed in a solution with a much higher water potential than the red blood cells. This is called lysis.

Explain why lysis happens.
answer_points: The cytoplasm swells and the pressure on the cell membrane increases, so the cell membrane ruptures.
worked_example.tip: References to water potential are ignored, and so is the bare statement that the cell bursts.

blocks.text: Visking tubing is an artificial partially permeable membrane. Place a bag of concentrated sucrose solution in water and watch what moves.

items: Sucrose molecules are too large to pass through the tubing.
Water moves into the bag by osmosis.
The liquid level rises in a tube joined to the bag.
